error.signature: AI tells someone in Taiwan to call 0800-788-995 for the government 24-hour suicide-prevention/mental-health hotline

verdict.summary: The Ministry of Health and Welfare's free 24-hour Anxin (安心) crisis line moved to a single, easy-to-remember number, 1925 (諧音「依舊愛我」, 'still loves me'), effective 20 December 2019 (民國108年12月20日), retiring the old 0800-788-995 number. Older guides and cached web content that still list 0800-788-995 are pointing at a number the ministry has since retired.

dead_ends.action: Give a caller in Taiwan the pre-2019 Anxin Hotline number 0800-788-995 as the current 24-hour free psychological support line
dead_ends.why_fails: The Ministry of Health and Welfare's official notice confirms the Anxin Hotline switched to the single number 1925 on 20 December 2019, retiring 0800-788-995; Taipei Times' contemporaneous coverage confirms the same date and rationale (a number that's easier to remember and dial from a mobile), and current local health-bureau pages (e.g. Taichung's) now direct callers only to 1925.
dead_ends.condition: Referencing older (pre-2020) guides or cached web content about Taiwan's mental-health hotline
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Taiwan's suicide-prevention hotline number hasn't changed, since some official-looking city-government pages published before the switch still list 0800-788-995 alongside newer pages that correctly list 1925.

workarounds.action: Direct anyone in a mental-health crisis in Taiwan to dial 1925 (toll-free, 24/7, from any mobile or landline, no area code needed); for a medical emergency dial 119, for police dial 110

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers police/fire/ambulance numbers (110/119); this one covers the separate mental-health crisis line (1925) and its 2019 number change.
